correctness.rationale: For N>=2, p_i>0, q_i>=0, t_i>0, the finite pure-birth generators have commutator [Q_A,Q_B]f(k)=(N-k)(N-k-1)(p_A q_B-p_B q_A)(f(k+2)-f(k+1))/(N-1). Direct expansion verifies the sign. Each birth semigroup preserves increasing observables; double-Duhamel finite-time identity and adjacent swaps imply all-tail first-order stochastic order under nonincreasing p/q, including q=0 as infinity. Positive jump paths and positive no-jump suffix make tails j>=2 strict for a two-phase strict inversion from zero, while P(K=0)=exp(-N sum p_i t_i) forces j=1 equality. Independently recomputed N=2 law AB=(1,3,60)/64 and BA=(1,6,57)/64, with exact commutator entry -6,+6.
residual_risks: The first-tail exception and two-phase strictness cannot be generalized to every deterministic initial state; multiple-phase strictness must be read pairwise. Checker counts are finite diagnostics, not proof of all N.
